market_holds: Spot $0.46 at the 2026-11-13 close (sealed baseline): a 52-week low, -92% from the 52-week high, -61% since the $1.19 close of 2026-09-30, and -39% below the $0.75 price of the 2026-09-30 registered direct offering (20m shares, $15m gross, proceeds 'to repay and/or restructure a portion of its convertible debt'; 8-K 2026-10-01). Market cap is about $56m on about 121.6m shares (101.63m on 2026-09-28 per the 424B5, plus 20m RDO). No usable option chain (ATM spread 100% of mid, IV ~306%), so the only size anchor is the history: median absolute reaction 17.2%, 7 of the last 8 reactions down (-22.8%, -11.7%, -29.5% on the last three). Short interest is 12.68m shares, ~12.6% of shares outstanding, 7.8 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30 via equibles, sweep row). The run-in is company-specific: the slide began with the RDO, and the 2026-11-11 date-change release ('to provide material updates on the status of its convertible debt discussions and other financing matters') coincided with a -7% day (0.515 to 0.477). Guide: FY26 revenue $100-115m and non-GAAP net loss $22-32m (Q2 release, 2026-08-13); Q3 'soft range' $24m to 'in excess of' $28m (CFO on the Q2 call). H1 revenue was $44.5m, so the low end of the FY guide needs about $27.7m a quarter in H2 against Q2's $24.3m. I found no current, dated sell-side consensus. The line the stock trades on is the $45.6m of 1.75% convertible notes that matured on 2026-11-15 (a Sunday), against $12.4m cash at 2026-06-30 and ~$11m a quarter of operating cash burn. My own arithmetic: equitizing the notes in full at about the current price leaves equity worth roughly what it trades at now, so the price already holds a heavily dilutive outcome.
view: This is a balance-sheet event wearing an earnings label. The release was moved from Nov 12 to 08:30 ET on Nov 16, the first business day after the converts matured, explicitly to report on the debt talks. Monday's release will settle which outcome holds: an agreed exchange or extension (dilutive but it removes the default tail), a forbearance or standstill while talks go on, or a payment default or court process. The company cannot repay at par from its own cash. By my estimate it holds roughly $15-20m after the RDO and Q3/Q4 burn, against $45.6m due. Management had said since August that it was 'in active discussions with our debt holders about potential restructuring', and the Oct 1 RDO was earmarked to 'repay and/or restructure a portion' of the notes. So the base case is a negotiated deal, probably announced alongside a weak Q3. Q3 revenue sits inside a $24-28m+ soft range that does not support the FY guide's $27.7m-a-quarter H2 ramp; VDR hyperscaler deals were 'not fully processed' and their timing 'not fully in our control'. A guide cut is more likely than not, and the going-concern language will stay. The price ($0.46, about $56m equity) already sits near a full-equitization value, so a deal with a noteholder haircut or a plain extension could bring a relief bounce, helped by 12.6% short interest. But 'status of discussions' is not 'completed transaction'. No 8-K for a signed exchange agreement has been filed up to Nov 13, and the outcomes outside a clean deal (forbearance, default, Chapter 11) are all sharply negative. With a negative skew and this stock's record of falling on its reports, I lean modestly down. I do not have the evidence to call it at 65%.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the outcome of the convertible-note talks, which matured Nov 15 and will be disclosed in the 08:30 ET release on Nov 16. The price has already fallen 61% since Sep 30 to about a full-equitization value, so a negotiated deal is not clearly unpriced in either direction. The negative skew (forbearance or default) and a likely guide cut lean down, but not to 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An exchange or extension in which noteholders take a material haircut or extend at par for little new equity, with no new discounted equity raise. That would remove the default tail at less dilution than the $0.46 price implies, and a 12.6% short base could squeeze it sharply up.

self_critique: Companies seldom delay a print to after a maturity unless they expect to announce a deal at the same time, and a signed exchange or extension that removes the bankruptcy tail at a price already at about full equitization could bring a sharp relief squeeze given 12.6% short interest and 7.8 days to cover. My negative lean leans partly on the stock's past reactions and an assumed guide cut, which matter less on a debt-resolution day. Equally, a Chapter 11 or a forbearance would make my -6% central estimate too mild.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line) and P4 (prove priced in) helped: the line is plainly the debt, and my own arithmetic suggested the price already sits near equitization value, which kept me off a short. P7's push to estimate the hidden line helped less here, because the outcome is a binary negotiation with no public inputs beyond the company's own wording.
